_: There are about 7,043 captive or farmed tigers, about 70 wild Siberian tigers, and about 14-20 wild Indochinese tigers. There are about 14 to 20 Indochinese tigers. There are about 8-10 wild Bengal tigers. There are 0 wild South China tigers.
Tiger populations was estimated to be 439 (192–996) and 393 (173–883), in 2008 and 2017.
The number of registered captive tigers, mostly in domestic private facilities, went up to 364 in 2021 from 97 in 2010.
After years of concerted conservation efforts, Thailand’s wild tiger populations are increasing, with a new estimate of 179-223 tigers.
Functionally extinct in 2016 due to poaching and habitat loss.
Captive tigers do still exist in Laos. Hundreds of genetically inbred big cats live in the country’s illegal tiger farms.
